note: The registry of every annotation Ipsissima reads. No new syntax: every key rides in Argdown's own front matter and {data} blocks, or in a source file's YAML front matter. tests/test_profile.py holds this file to what the checker and the app actually read.

defaults.summary: Claim metadata declared once for every claim that does not set its own (usually `chapter`); `reviewed` here records a person's pass over the whole map.

contentions.summary: The text's stated theses, added to the computed apex. Only the author's own.

questions.summary: The questions the text works on, in its words or the reconstructor's: what its claims answer, reframe, split or dissolve (since 1.17). In a question's `text`, words in double quotation marks inside the value are the text's own and are verified like any quotation; words without them are the reconstructor's (since 1.22).

frames.type: map of id to {kind, label, pinpoint, values, ordered, comparable, rule, question, note}, or none
frames.summary: The comparisons the text itself makes: its cases (rows), the dimensions and verdict it gives them (columns, with the text's values), and the rival accounts of one thing it sets against each other. Claims are placed in them with `about:`. Read with every reconstruction since 1.21 (a trial from 20 Oct 2026); `none` records that the text compares nothing. In a label or a value's label, words in double quotation marks inside the value are the text's own and are verified like any quotation; words without them are the reconstructor's (since 1.22). `comparable: false` on a dimension records that the text says its cells do not measure one thing across the cases: the page shows them and never compares them (since 1.24). An account frame names the declared question its accounts answer, `question: <id>` (since 1.26).

text-provenance.summary: Declares that the manuscript itself was machine-generated; shown beside the title.

author.summary: Who drew a survey map (a map with no source text).

draft.summary: As the reading policy's `draft`, read here too, where older maps put it.

date.summary: When a survey map was drawn.

mechanism.summary: The causal chain the text asserts.

generated.summary: A model wrote the map; the checker may correct its fidelity markers.

draft.summary: The text is still being written; findings about unfinishedness become observations.

aim.summary: fit: what the text says; appropriation: the best philosophy in it.

unit.summary: Which sense of the words, or which view is held.

method.summary: How the map's mechanism was reconstructed: series (argument first, then the mechanism pass) or parallel (argument and mechanism read together, the mechanism entering the argument through bridges). Since 1.15.

strength.summary: How much better than their words the author is assumed to be.

chapter.summary: The source file the claim reads, relative to the source root.

section.summary: The heading in that file the claim belongs to.

source.summary: A quotation pinning a claim whose own text is a summary; verified like any quotation.

echoes.summary: Where else the text states the claim -- its thesis announced in the abstract, say -- as the author's words. Verified like any quotation; never pins the claim, which stays where it is argued.

pinpoint.summary: Where a reader finds it in print: p. 12, pp. 34, 36, [50].

line.summary: The line in the chapter the claim is placed at, where no quotation places it.

fidelity.summary: How far the claim's own text stands from the author's words.

warrant.summary: Why a departure (interpretation, imputation) is allowed.

note.summary: What the notation cannot carry: the limitation, the reading followed, the road not taken.

reviewed.summary: The date a person reviewed the claim. Never set by a model.

causes.summary: The causal step(s) the claim states.

question.type: {id, move, into} or a list of them
question.summary: What the claim does to a declared question: answers it; reframes it, or splits it, `into` the question(s) that take its place; or dissolves it, showing it has no answer to give. A reframing is a move on a question, not a reason (since 1.17).

mechanism.summary: The claim states a declared chain as a whole -- the account the text gives -- and stands for it in the argument: supported as one account, attacked by a rival, a premise of a bridge, where its steps count as the premise's. `true` stands for the whole mechanism of a map with no chains (since 1.20).

constitutes.summary: The constitutive relation(s) the claim states: what makes a whole up, never walked as a step (since 1.11).

inconsistent.summary: The claim is one of a set the text says cannot all hold (a trilemma, a dilemma, a trade-off): every member carries the same name. The reader is asked which they would give up, and shown what each would cost (since 18 Oct 2026).

about.type: map of frame to value, or a list of them
about.summary: The cell or cells of the text's own comparisons that the claim states: its case, and the value it gives on a dimension declared under `frames:` (since 20 Oct 2026; part of every reconstruction since 1.21). Reserved values, on a dimension or a verdict: `impossible` and `indeterminate`, what the text says of a cell instead of a value; alone on an account frame, `indeterminate` marks a reason the text says does not tell the accounts apart (since 1.23).

uses.summary: Which premises the step uses; required where a structure has two or more steps.

formalization.summary: The line's logical form, in NLTK syntax.

formalized.summary: The stamp of the words the formula was read against, written by a person with --stamp.

isGroup.summary: Argdown's own: the heading groups its claims.

tags.reported: a view the text sets out but does not hold
tags.conceded: something the author grants tells against them
tags.contested: an objection voiced in the text that is not the author's view
tags.authority: a proposition whose force comes from its source, not its content
tags.obiter: said in a judgment, but not a necessary step to the disposal
tags.crux: a claim the reconstructor settled by choosing among live readings
tags.appraisal: the reconstructor's own reading of the text against the world

bridges.summary: Causal schemes an inference line may name (`-- From consequences {uses: [1, 2]} --`) where a step-bearing claim serves as a premise: a BRIDGE from the mechanism into the argument. A scheme names a defeasible causal move, not a deductive rule, and is never checked for validity. Since 1.15; transfer and the vindicating and contingent genealogies since 1.16, from the parallel-pass trial (1 Oct 2026); after Walton, Reed and Macagno, Argumentation Schemes (2008). Each question's `asks` names what the map can say about it (the census's probe: `counter`, `rivals`, `blockers` and the rest, docs/PROFILE.md), or null where only a reader can answer it; since 10 Oct 2026.

schemes.name: From cause to effect
schemes.move: The steps bring the effect about, so it will or does occur.
questions: How strong is each step, and what backs it?
Does anything stated block or counteract the effect (unless, a rival route, a regime)?

schemes.name: From effect to cause
schemes.move: The mechanism best explains what was observed.
questions: Which rival accounts does the text set out?
How thorough is the account: where does the chain stop?

schemes.name: From correlation to cause
schemes.move: Two things go together, so one brings the other about.
questions: Is there a common cause?
Could it run the other way?
Is it mediated, and over what range does it hold?
Is the measure itself the source of the change?

schemes.name: From cases to a general mechanism
schemes.move: The steps hold in these cases, so the general step holds.
questions: Are the cases kinds of the general step?
How many cases, and how different?
Is a general claim drawn from one case?

schemes.name: From there to here
schemes.move: A conclusion established in one setting -- a study population, a case, a thought experiment, a model, another country -- is carried to another, because the mechanism that produced it is shared.
questions: Is the mechanism of action present here?
Are its support factors (its `jointly` and `given` conditions) said to hold here?
Is there a counteracting mechanism here that was absent there?
For a stipulated case: what did it stipulate that the world does not have?
For a normative conclusion: does the consideration keep its weight and polarity here?

schemes.name: From a mechanism to what to do
schemes.move: A route runs from an action to a valued outcome, so the action should be taken.
questions: What other goals does the action bear on?
What other routes reach the goal?
Can the action be taken: does anything block it?
What other consequences does it have?

schemes.name: From consequences
schemes.move: A route runs to a good or bad outcome, so the policy, rule or view is good or bad.
questions: Does the route exist in the text?
What other consequences does the text give?
What criterion of good or bad does the step rely on?

schemes.name: From a mechanism to a possibility
schemes.move: The mechanism has a lever, so things can be otherwise.
questions: Does anything block the lever?
Is the outcome only possible, or open?

schemes.name: From a mechanism against a theory
schemes.move: A mechanism the theory denies or ignores holds, so the theory fails.
questions: Does the mechanism hold where the theory claims to hold (scope, regime, conditions)?

schemes.name: From a mechanism to a classification
schemes.move: What the mechanism does makes the case one of a kind (forced, momentous, brittle).
questions: Does the mechanism establish each condition the kind requires?

schemes.name: Genealogical debunking
schemes.move: A view is produced by a cause that does not track its truth, so its claim to authority fails.
questions: Is the producing cause one that could not track the truth?
Does the critique apply to the critic's own view?

schemes.name: Vindicatory genealogy
schemes.move: A practice or view came about because it meets needs we have, so it merits our confidence.
questions: Does the process that formed it give reasons to prefer it over its rivals, including giving it up?
Whose needs are these, and do we share and endorse them?
Do the needs the story starts from still hold for us?
Is the story's order historical, or the order in which complications are added?

schemes.name: From a genealogy to contingency
schemes.move: A practice or view came about by a process that gives no reason to prefer it over its rivals, so it is rationally contingent: it could as well have been otherwise.
questions: Does the formation process really give no reason to prefer it?
Is contingency being taken as a reason against it, which it is not?
Would a rival have met the same needs as well?

levels.summary: Levels of social complexity, top first.

ordering.type: composition | space | authority | scale | sequence | systems | mixed | unstated, or {kind, pinpoint}
ordering.summary: What kind of ordering the levels are; the reconstructor's reading unless a pinpoint shows where the text says it (since 1.10).

within.summary: Each level's parent, where the levels nest: a tree, siblings side by side within their parent (since 1.10).

goal.summary: What the chain is for: to explain why and how, to find what to do, to predict, or to attribute responsibility. Also on each chain (since 1.13).

contrast.summary: The foil the question sets: why this, rather than what. Also on each chain (since 1.13).

keys.label: string
keys.general: a state id of this kind: the general claim, of which the kind's other states are cases (since 1.7)

kinds.summary: Kinds of state that recur across cases; states of one kind are never walked as one (since 1.6).

depth.summary: How far the mechanism is mapped: in full; as a sketch, the question, actors and chains with steps only where the argument relies on them; or considered and not mapped. Under the parallel method every map records it (since 1.17).

depth_reason.summary: Why a mechanism is a sketch or not mapped, in a line (since 1.17).

keys.label: string
keys.question: string
keys.roles: map of state id to a role or list of roles: the role the state plays in this chain
keys.form: chain | cycle: this chain's own form (since 1.11)
keys.apart: string: why the text keeps this chain, or its pieces, apart from the rest (since 1.18)

chains.summary: Several chains the text sets out, each answering its own question (since 1.5).

keys.label: string
keys.actor: an actor id, or (since 1.12) a list of them: a relation or a doing of several actors together; may be left out where `levels` places a process with no owner (since 1.11)
keys.status: actual | possible | open: whether the state is actual, a possibility the text sets out, or what the text says cannot be specified in advance (since 1.12)
keys.aspect: quantity | activity | development | event | condition: what kind of occurrence the state is, from the text's own grammar (since 1.11)
keys.role: intervention | condition | outcome, or a list of them (condition and lists since 1.1)
keys.part_of: a state id: the whole this state is a part, facet or instance of (since 1.2)
keys.levels: a list of levels: the levels a state holds at, when more than its actor's; drawn across them (since 1.4)
keys.kind: a kind id: the declared kind this state is a case of (since 1.6)
keys.measures: a state id: the state this one is a measure, indicator or estimate of -- a reading of it, never walked as its cause (since 1.9)
keys.method: string: how that measure is taken, in the text's words (since 1.9)

sign.summary: + raises, - lowers, "0" a finding of no effect, which decides which alternative follows (since 1.2).

basis.summary: What the text offers for the step.

period.summary: When the step holds, in the text's words anchored to an event: during culling, after it ended (since 1.8).

on.type: level | trend | being | persistence | character | possibility | chance | stock
on.summary: Whether the step moves the level of its `to` (the default) or its trend: slows a rise, speeds a fall (since 1.8); or (since 1.11) makes or unmakes it (being, + or -), maintains or erodes it (persistence, + or -), or changes what kind of thing it is (character, with sign: which); or (since 1.12) opens or closes the possibility of it (possibility, + or -); or (since 1.14) makes it more or less likely (chance, + or -), or flows into or out of it, a stock (stock, + or -): an inflow or an outflow, which the stock need not move with.

given.summary: Conditions the text states, in its words, or (since 1.8) a declared state and the value it has.

selects.summary: A selection link: who ends up on each side, not an effect.

hedged.summary: The text puts the step as a possibility.

chain.type: chain id or list of chain ids
chain.summary: Which declared chain(s) the step belongs to (since 1.5).

jointly.type: state id or list of state ids
jointly.summary: The step holds only together with these states: a joint cause (since 1.4).

unless.type: state id or list of state ids
unless.summary: The step holds unless these states hold: a blocker, walked as a cause of the opposite sign (since 1.8).

regime.summary: The regime the step holds in, in the text's words: a dose, a place, a model. Routes are composed only within one regime (since 1.8).

threshold.summary: The threshold the step acts past, in the text's words: the step is not a monotone rise or fall (since 1.8).

size.type: string or {value, unit, ci, versus, at}
size.summary: The magnitude the text gives for the step, quoted: an effect size, with its interval, comparison and time (since 1.8).

via.type: state id or list of state ids
via.summary: The finer route the text opens this step into, in order: the step IS that route, walked once (since 1.8).

modifies.type: {by, effect, period}, or a list of them
modifies.summary: A state that moderates the step: `effect` strengthens, weakens or reverses it, or -- "0" -- the text finds it does not moderate it. The moderator is linked by the step, never walked as a cause (since 1.9).

necessary.summary: The step's `to` holds only where its `from` does: "only if". Drawn "needed for", not "raises" (since 1.9).

sufficient.summary: `true`: the cause, with any `jointly` co-causes, brings the effect about on its own. `false`: the text says it is not enough on its own (since 1.9).

design.summary: The design of the evidence for the step, in the text's words; these values are read, others kept as written. `illustration` is a hypothetical case, shaded as asserted (since 1.9).

attribution.summary: The type of causing the step attributes, after Stone (1989): purposeful or not, intended or not, guided through another agent, or a web with no single locus; `by` names the actor whose action or intention it is (since 1.9).

measured_by.type: state id or list of state ids
measured_by.summary: The measure the step's evidence is read from: a state with `measures`. A step into that measure other than from what it measures is a bias that bears on the evidence, drawn as an undercut (since 1.9).

stance.summary: On a #reported or #contested step: whether the text sets out the view to reject it or leaves it unjudged. A report the text endorses is a claim in its own voice, not a stance (since 1.9).

association.summary: The text reports that the two go together and does not say one brings the other about: drawn without a head, never walked; the census names any common cause drawn (since 1.13).

scope.summary: Whether the step is about a particular case or a general relation between kinds or variables (since 1.13).

name.summary: The step's name in the text's words -- the kind of mechanism it is, the question it asks, the feedback it is -- drawn on the arrow in place of the verb (since 1.19).

mark.summary: A short label the text numbers the step by ("1", "P4"), drawn in a circle on the arrow; six characters at most (since 1.19).

from.summary: What makes the whole up, wholly or partly.

to.summary: The whole: a state, or an actor -- a group or a system that the ongoing states constitute.

extent.summary: Whether it constitutes part of the whole or all of it.

whole.summary: How the whole stands to what constitutes it: no more than their sum; dependent on their organisation; nothing but them; or (since 1.12) each making the other.

basis.summary: What the text offers: as for a step, or an account's judgement, or a definition.

stance.summary: On a #reported or #contested claim, as for a step.

constitutes.summary: A constitutive relation (since 1.11): what a whole is made up of, carried by a claim as a step is. Never walked, never composed with steps, never drawn as an arrow; cycles are allowed. A pair may be related both causally and constitutively.

retired.summary: Keys profile 1.25 retired (22 Oct 2026, on James's ruling): added one trial at a time, used in almost no ordinary map, and unlikely to be plain to a reader. An old map that carries one opens as before; the key is not read, and the checker and the editor say what to write instead.

account.instead: nothing: say in the question or a claim how the text reasons about causes, where it matters

form.instead: `form: cycle` on the chain that is a cycle

settles.instead: `settles:` on the chain that is a cycle

order.instead: nothing: where a genealogy's stages are not the order of time, say so in the chain's question

idiom.instead: a sentence in the mechanism's `question`, or a state's `note`

apart.instead: `apart:` on the chain the text keeps apart

boundary.instead: a claim, where the text argues where its system stops

channels.instead: chains for the kinds of link the text tells apart, or a state's `note`

account.instead: nothing: say in the chain's question how the text reasons about causes, where it matters

order.instead: nothing: say in the chain's question that its stages are not the order of time

boundary.instead: a claim, where the text argues where the chain's system stops

conditioned.instead: `given:` on the steps the analysis holds fixed

dead_end.instead: `role: outcome`, where the text sets the state out as where the process stops

despite.instead: the claim's words (`given:` would say the step holds only where the state does)

share.instead: `via:` alone, with how much of the step runs by the route in the claim's words

channel.instead: the step's `chain:`, or the claim's words

licence.summary: An SPDX identifier where there is one.

abstract.summary: The text's own abstract, shown on the orientation panel.

voice.summary: For a wholly dramatised text: whose voice the mapped argument is in.

facts.summary: For a judgment: the facts of the case.

attribution.summary: For a pasted text: whose it is.

zotero.summary: The Zotero attachment key the text was converted from.

source_markup.back_matter: the first heading of References, Notes, Bibliography and their kin; kept in the file, never quoted as argument
source_markup.project_file: chapters: a list of files, optionally grouped under `part:`; Quarto's `book: chapters:` is read the same way

folded: runs of whitespace, the non-breaking space among them
single, double, curly and straight quotation marks and guillemets, all as one
en and em dashes, as a hyphen
the ellipsis character, as three stops
